newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FORECAST-Hardie year net profit seen down.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Hardie year net profit seen down.

text.p: Building materials group James Hardie Industries Ltd is expected to announce its second consecutive annual net profit fall this week due to tough conditions in the domestic housing market.

Analysts contactedexpect Hardie to report on Thursday a pre-abnormal net profit of between A$50 million and A$53 million for 1996/97 to March 31 compared with A$58.4 million in 1995/96. The company is expected to pay a final dividend of 6.5 cents, unchanged from last year and making 13 cents for the year.
BZW Australia forecasts a pre-abnormal net profit of A$51 million for the 1996/97 year.
Fabian Babich, building materials analyst at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, forecasts a pre-abnormal net profit of A$50 million with an unchanged final dividend.
One Sydney analyst forecast a 1996/97 net profit before abnormals of A$53 million, but said he would not be surprised if the group reported a lower figure.

The 1996/97 results are likely to show an abnormal profit following the sale of around A$430 milllion in assets during the year. The assets sold include Hardie's interests in theme parks, bathroom products, irrigation and fire protection.
At the release of the 1996/97 half year results, Hardie managing director Keith Barton said he expected the second half result to be significantly down on the first half.
Hardie, about 28 percent owned by Brierley Investments Ltd, reported a 12.1 percent fall in net profit before abnormals to A$27.6 million for half year to September 30.
"People are not really looking at this year. Next year is the key, that is when we expect to see some significant results coming through," the Sydney analyst said.
Analysts said the 1997/98 turnaround would be driven by stronger activity in the Australian housing market and increased contributions from operations in the United States.

However, analysts said company executives have recently been telling analysts to ratchet down 1997/98 forecasts to around A$80 million to A$85 million from about A$90 million and above earlier this year.
